model_params.model_per_bearing: one Isolation Forest per bearing on that bearing's channel features (1 channel(s) x rms/std/kurtosis/crest/peak = 5 features)
model_params.threshold: 0.95 quantile of the bearing's own train-window anomaly scores
model_params.sustained_alarm_definition: score above threshold for >= 10 consecutive snapshots
model_params.protocol_identity: protocol constants and the sustained-alarm helper are imported from run_wave5_ims (the Test 1 runner) — identical protocol by construction

split.protocol: TEMPORAL split within one run-to-failure test: each bearing's detector is fitted ONLY on the first 30% of snapshots (early life, nominal by construction) and scored over the full run. No random splitting anywhere — snapshot order is the run's chronology. Identical to the wave-5 Test 1 protocol.

preprocessing.feature_note: per-snapshot per-channel time-domain features from IMSAdapter; no scaling (tree model), no fitted statistics of any kind beyond the detector itself and its train-window threshold
preprocessing.channels: 4 = 4 bearings x 1 accelerometer; column k = bearing k
preprocessing.channel_difference_vs_test1: Tests 2-3 recorded ONE accelerometer per bearing (4 channels total); Test 1 recorded two per bearing (8 channels). Each bearing's detector here therefore uses 5 features instead of 10 — a property of the recorded data, stated rather than corrected.

metrics.framing: ALARM TIMING ONLY. IMS 3rd_test has no per-snapshot labels; the only ground truth is the teardown finding (bearing 3 outer-race failure; the other bearings none reported). Classification scores are therefore NOT computable and are not reported.

notes: IMS 3rd_test integrated in wave 9, completing the IMS dataset (Tests 1-3) under the identical wave-5 protocol. Detectors see only their own bearing's channels. A sustained alarm on bearing 3 (the documented failure) late in the run, with the other bearings quiet or much later, is the success pattern this design can honestly show; whatever the measured pattern is, it is reported as measured in EXPERIMENTS_REPORT.md. Data is real run-to-failure rig data (not field data); licence not stated on the PCoE page.

archive_provenance.extracted_scope: 3rd_test extracted in wave 9 from the local archive retained since wave 5 (no re-download needed)

reference_test1_wave5.note: Test 1 detectors used 10 features per bearing (2 channels); Tests 2-3 use 5 (1 channel) — alarm timings are comparable as protocol outcomes, not as identical-feature results
